features.label: Interactive answers
features.description: Assistant replies can include an interactive card written in OpenUI Lang inside an openui code fence (38 components: layout, metrics, tables, line/area/bar/pie charts, tabs, checklists, inputs that recompute on the page), built up statement by statement while the reply streams; buttons and choices send a follow-up message; Query()/Mutation() read and (with an Allow each time) change data through the user's MCP connectors. When components can't do it, an ```app fence draws a small HTML/JS app inline in the reply, in the MCP sandbox proxy with no network, themed with --viz-* variables and watched by a heartbeat. allternit-api checks each finished reply's cards against the catalog (card_check frame: diagnostics + text fallback) and stores the checks and the user's card state per message (message_card_meta). The app sends the model manual with every chat turn unless Settings says Text only; channels get cards as readable text and apps as one line.

decisions.note: Renderer shipped on the polish primitives, with deterministic local state via OpenUI $state and no eval. The model-side prompt is a separate session by Eoj's call: no per-model testing, no training.

The app (not gizzi-code) sends the manual as systemPrompt / '+' system, so each build only asks for components it renders and the TUI and channels never get it. Settings → Response style → Layout and visuals (Auto / Text only) is per device, like the Memory switches, to avoid a manual prod migration.

Live data through the MCP Apps bridge: Query() only on read-only tools, writes only as a Mutation() from a button with an Allow bar every time. OpenUI Gateway and observability-cloud are not used (owned infra; no data to Thesys). react-lang pinned to 0.3.1 to respect pnpm's minimum release age.

Removed the [v:...] pseudo-syntax, AllternitOpenUIRenderer/registry, BlueprintCanvas, the test-only code-compiler and the fake render_walkthrough tool. Design mode previews the reply's card with DESIGN.md tokens; UI Forge is the card playground.

Parity pass against ChatGPT Intelligent UI: progressive card streaming (complete statements only), per-part error boundaries with text fallback, catalog 16→38 with model-nameable design tokens, ```app inline apps through the sandbox proxy (process-isolated, heartbeat watchdog), server-side card checks and per-message card state that follows the user across devices. Model JSX and legacy sandbox parts now run in the inline-app sandbox instead of the page; the A2UI extended renderer and backend client, @allternit/ix, and the json-render and react-jsx-parser deps were removed as dead code.

decisions.note: Eoj, 2026-10-17: Allternit Desktop bundles and runs the subscription gateway (subs-gateway-manager.ts; scripts/prepare-subs-gateway.cjs → resources/subs-gateway, node:sqlite so no native module, Electron's Node, ~/.allternit/subscriptions with the file secret store; skipped where ALLTERNIT_LOCAL_SUBS_GATEWAY=1 already). allternit-api ALLTERNIT_LOCAL_SUBS_GATEWAY=fallback: a bound, running, allowed Sessions computer answers first, else Desktop's own gateway; =1 (cloud computer image) stays primary; /subscriptions/status reports local, fallback and sessions_computer. D15 becomes a lane rule: phone and desktop-app lanes run on the person's own computer; browser lanes there are off until turned on (GET/PUT /v1/settings/browser-lanes; off = no browser account routes, web route offline, login 409 browser_lanes_off) and then run in the installed Google Chrome — never Chrome for Testing (OpenAI geoblocks it, too many checks) — headless=new on the account's profile, automation features off, Chrome's normal user agent (HeadlessChrome is held by Cloudflare; live check on chatgpt.com passed), attached over CDP (worker/hidden_chrome.ts). Model-picker chats (POST /v1/tasks chat.create/continue with a provider) ask the same RouteDirector at turn start; phone/desktop-app routes run through the route's AAI adapter (routes/app-route-tasks.ts) with worker-identical task events, thread → app conversation persisted (migration 0013); NO_ROUTE keeps the FabricRouter browser path. Pairing handover to a Sessions computer: Mac → Sessions computer only (approve-on-phone is a future note, not built).

Deterministic route router for signed-in apps (spec P0 + the Settings API): six routes in a fixed order (android-app -> iphone-app-ictrl -> desktop-app-cdp -> desktop-app-ax -> web -> iphone-app-usb-agent), selected by a pure function of (vendor, eligible routes, order, override) and logged with its reason. A route is eligible only when signed in, online, and every capability-contract item (§3, 7 items) passed the /aai/conformance suite for the CURRENT app version — results stored per (vendor, route, app_version); an app update re-arms ineligibility until the suite re-runs. The chosen route is written into the vendor's binding; the AAI host consults the router only at turn start, so failover is strictly between-turn and a streaming turn never switches; no eligible route answers the typed NO_ROUTE ("phone offline, no other signed-in route") — never a weaker fallback. desktop-app-cdp applies only while the shipped app accepts its debug flag unmodified (launch-time probe per app version; never patch/re-sign/inject a vendor binary — otherwise desktop-app-ax or the phone). Settings API: GET /v1/routes + PUT /v1/routes/:vendor/override (400 unless eligible). Phone routes register now but their adapters are a follow-up task: eligible stays false with the failing items until conformance passes — never assumed. Gateway-local: services/subscription-gateway/src/routes/* (registry, contract, select, store, director), migration 0012, test/routes-router.test.ts.

Gap closure: website/app products need the person's consent once per account (needs_consent); extra turns on one website/desktop subscription queue in order with a visible status instead of failing; AAI contexts persist across gateway restarts; GET /aai/events/stream (SSE); one broken adapter no longer blocks the rest; Managed Agents streams events and answers custom tools (POST /threads/:id/gateway/tool-result); bots with no allowlist ask before shell, writes and web fetches (GIZZI_BOT_BYPASS_PERMISSIONS=1 restores the old default). Live vendor verification remains an owner-run gate (scripts/e2e/gateway-live-check.sh).

One-step POST /gateway/connect replaces the manual account/state/discover/bind/READY walk; the step-by-step wizard stays as the advanced path. Only Grok Bot is verified live; the web-subscription and dots lanes are offline-verified only.

features.label: Computer toolset for every model
features.description: Two contract generations (allternit.computer.v1 + allternit.browser.v1, and allternit.computer.v2: the v1 pixel members plus ten driver-backed structured members) and one executor (POST /computers/:id/toolset) that every gizzi model adapter and both published computer-driver SDKs call: Claude-native toolsets, OpenAI, Gemini and JSON function tools. Lease, approval, audit and coordinate scaling happen in one place.

decisions.note: Eoj: computer use works for every model. Anthropic's toolsets are absorbed as one adapter into our contract, gizzi stays the only loop, and there are no hosted third-party drivers. The old gizzi browser tool (goal-driven, a second loop) was removed in favour of the toolset browser tool.

Member gaps closed: the browser gateway runs all 31 members (refs, tabs with browser_state, console, network, JS, upload) through /v1/toolset/browser with an http(s)-only URL policy and public-only hosts for cloud targets; Windows guests run all 17 computer members through PowerShell/user32; this Mac gets cursor_position, modifier clicks and emulated mouse down/up. hold_key on macOS stays off: Cua Driver 0.34 has no hold call there. Optional browser members need an explicit enable.

D1: the Allternit Driver sidecar (domains/computer-use/driver) sits between allternit-api and the OS: a forked arc-driver (macOS AX reads, settle, freshness guard, menus) and Cua Driver 0.34 (all OS) behind one JSON-RPC API, with our own element ids and map versions, a learned per-op router, and one reader and one input owner per window. This-device input goes through its pixel_* ops; the Desktop app launches it with a bundled Python.

D2: contract v2 (allternit.computer.v2) ships — the 17 pixel members plus read_ui/act/run_batch/verify through the driver sidecar, request_human (lease pause, live view with input enabled, POST /api/v1/computers/:id/human-done resume) and use_credential (sealed vault + macOS Keychain + Bitwarden/1Password CLI adapters + RFC 6238 TOTP; values never enter the model context or logs; optional app/domain bindings). gizzi offers the structured members as the computer_v2 function tool to every model family (Claude keeps its native toolset for the pixel members). Windows this-device input moves off the Cua CLI fallback onto the sidecar over token-gated loopback TCP.

E4: live element map in the driver (allternit_driver/live). One AXObserver per app on one run-loop thread feeds arc's journal, settle counter and walk caches plus the map; notifications patch the map incrementally (full walk only on first sight, window-level changes, big bursts, or a failed staleness probe), so a re-read is answered with no accessibility call (0.4-0.5 ms median through the socket on this Mac). Windows are watched on demand, unwatched after 5 min idle, capped at 8; apps without notifications degrade to timed narrow reads and say so. Linux (AT-SPI over D-Bus, jeepney) and Windows (UIA, comtypes) observers are written to the same interface and staged by prepare-allternit-driver.cjs, unverified live until a non-production test machine exists. The macOS sidecar now runs the Cocoa main run loop so apps launched after it starts are found.

D5/E3 safety layer (computer_safety.rs): one assessment per toolset call and run_subtask step. Untrusted observations spotlighted (nonce-delimited, secrets scrubbed); per-step /v1/decisions monitor of kind safety on mutating non-sandbox steps (fast tiers, fail-closed to confirm when unsure or failed, absent when no fast tier; read-only steps never wait on it); one irreversible classifier (send/pay/purchase/transfer/delete/publish/credentials/account) shared with run_subtask, always confirmed on every target; watch mode on email/banking/admin apps and sites (computer.safety events, mutating steps confirmed); per-computer and owner-default app/domain allow/deny lists (V246, GET/PUT /computers/:id/safety); vault secrets screened on every free-text path against their bind; screenshot redaction by driver OCR before images leave the executor; VM snapshot before the first risky step of a run on cloud computers.

D4: replay cache (Stagehand design over the driver element map). run_subtask keys each subtask on hash(goal, app + window shape, input names) per owner (computer_replays, V248); the first run records semantic locators (element id, role, name, tree path, window-relative box, 8x8 pixel hash) plus a verify check per step once the exact success checks hold; later runs replay in one speculative run_batch with zero decisions, re-find a moved element by name/path/pixels or re-infer it with one decision, and rewrite the entry. Input values are never stored ({{name}} placeholders plus a guard). save_as turns a recording into a named skill; run_skill and skills (contract v2 members) run and list them. read_ui gains paths and crops.

D6: vision fallback in the driver (allternit_driver/vision). Router.choose_source decides per window read: ax, vision (empty/sparse tree, tree error) or hybrid (tree plus marks inside opaque canvas-like regions), recorded per app and audited. Set-of-marks from Apple Vision OCR plus a model-free edge-blob proposer become v-prefixed elements (source vision, mark n) that act/run_batch/verify take like tree ids; vision act is desktop pixel input behind a mean-hash freshness check. read_ui target grounds a description with the local grounder (UI-Venus-1.5-8B MLX 4-bit primary, Holo2-8B fallback, both Apache-2.0) with zoom-and-reground on low confidence. Packages install into the state dir on first use; the model runs in a child vision worker, unloaded after 10 min idle; a vLLM endpoint (ALLTERNIT_GROUNDER_URL) is the cloud seam, configuration only. Cua parse_visual_regions is not used (needs AGPL cua-perception).

K2: generate.mjs also emits the published SDK bindings (sdk/computer-driver/src/v2-generated.ts and sdk/computer-driver/python/allternit_computer_driver/_v2_types.py), covered by the same --check drift gate, so the SDKs' v2 types track this contract instead of drifting.

K4 safety gaps closed. Screenshot redaction no longer depends on a host driver: when no driver OCR is available (a cloud-hosted allternit-api), a built-in pure-Rust OCR engine (ocrs, MIT/Apache-2.0, rten inference) redacts server-side. Its models fetch once into the data dir on first use, pinned by URL and checked against a pinned SHA-256, the engine runs off the async runtime with a 40 MB PNG / 4096x4096 px cap and a timeout, and its word boxes feed the same find_pii + blackout code as the driver; a guest computer's own driver OCR slots in ahead of the server engine when the guest image ships it (computer_ocr.rs). App/domain allow/deny lists gain project scope (V250): settings resolve computer -> project -> owner default through SafetySettings::over, written with cowork_projects ownership verification at GET/PUT /projects/:id/safety; a toolset call's project is its run's session project (the a_run_id session link), a wire project_id is verified against the owner's projects and the run's project, and a mismatch refuses the call.

D1b (task K5): the Allternit Driver ships in every guest image (Linux systemd service, Windows logon task, container, tart VMs, Firecracker rootfs), and allternit-api routes the structured members (read_ui, act, run_batch, verify) for Target::Guest through the guest exec channel via the in-guest forwarder (cmd/allternit-api/src/guest_driver.rs). The static "unimplemented until the guest driver image ships" refusals are gone: a guest whose driver does not answer fails as driver_unavailable, and pixel members use the driver path first with xdotool/scrot/PowerShell as the explicit fallback.

features.label: Decision Runtime (typed decisions)
features.description: POST /v1/decisions (alias /v1/systemone) in allternit-api's Agency Kernel: one choice over up to 255 caller options, answered by the owned local scorer (one-pass option scoring on MLX or llama.cpp, Qwen3.5-4B), escalating under a per-kind threshold to optional vendor adapters (off by default, per project) and the planner model through gizzi, within a latency budget, with abstain. Every decision and its outcome is stored (V245 decisions). The flywheel (V247) runs registered heads in shadow, promotes/demotes them on outcome accuracy with hysteresis and an audit trail, and serves live heads first (head.lookup: exact-match over past outcomes, <10 ms). GET/PUT /v1/decisions/heads.

decisions.note: E1: the Decision Runtime lives in the Agency Kernel slot (no second runtime). open-jev's one-pass scoring is ported as an owned sidecar; Qwen3.5-4B is the default (Apache-2.0, no HF login), Gemma 3 4B a config switch. Packages and weights install on first use; nothing heavy ships in the app. Training our own model is the separate M track.

E2: computer use runs on typed decisions. run_subtask (allternit.computer.v2, every model family via computer_v2) takes a goal, literal inputs, verify-syntax success checks, constraints and limits; the executor loop (computer_subtask.rs) reads the live element map with since diffs, builds element x op options plus done/escalate, decides on the fast tiers only (no oracle), runs each step through lease/policy/audit (predictable typing batched with expect checks), checks success with verify, hands back to the planner with a compact screen when a decision abstains, and writes every outcome back to the decision store. Driver: text entry writes AXValue instead of arc's SkyLight focus-borrowing, which crashed the sidecar on macOS 14.

E5 + E6: flywheel framework only (training stays in the M track, which registers trained heads through the same Head trait). Promotion is judged on accuracy against reported outcomes (default 97% over 200 labelled, not overconfident), demotion under 93%, metrics reset at each transition; safety heads never auto-promote; manual moves only for ALLTERNIT_DECISIONS_ADMINS. Vendor adapters follow the vendors' published docs (hosted decisions API public beta; TypeSafe Jev /v1/systemone), gated by key AND per-project enable (ALLTERNIT_DECISIONS_VENDOR_PROJECTS); not exercised live (metered). compare_backends.py gives a same-decisions latency/accuracy table and refuses metered backends without --allow-metered.

D7: run_parallel runs independent subtasks on separate computers at once (per-computer target/lease/audit, one input owner per computer via a process-wide registry, max_parallel/budget_ms/max_cost_usd); run_subtask best_of N runs N rollouts on N sandbox computers only (refused on the person's own machine) and a judge decision picks one by step narratives (computer_parallel.rs). run_subtask api_options offers the planner's MCP/API calls ahead of GUI steps (status use_api). Subtasks on cloud computers wait for the guest driver image (D1b).

features.label: Custom project and folder icons
features.description: Personal folder recipes with 48 symbols, 71 brand marks, color, paper layers, text/emoji and raster logos; project Details and bot project headers have independently configurable banners with 20 presets and custom hues.

decisions.note: Eoj approved the iFolder-inspired customization and requested merge/push. Recipes are personal preferences on the connected runtime; no OS icon or execution-setting changes.
Integrated with the current PreviewCard polish layout; customization stays in the card options menu. Runtime API tests are added, not locally compiled under the no-build instruction.
Expanded searchable catalogs, drag/drop image import, hover/focus rail controls, and appearance-derived project header banners on all shared surfaces.
Project Details and bot project banners have independent saved bannerColor with the same 20 presets as bot banners and custom hue selection.
Project homes and Details now share a full-width bot-style banner; compact two-column appearance editor keeps Save and Cancel visible with a scrollable phone body.

Unified Appearance/Configuration project dialog across modes, explicit compact geometry and scrolling, adaptive symbol cells. Bot phone Workspace & Config uses panel container sizing, horizontal file tabs and stacked cards.

features.label: Artifacts (one typed store, versions, sharing)
features.description: Artifacts v2: one account-level store of typed artifacts (doc, sheet, slides, design, dashboard, motion, page, card, diagram, image, code, pdf) in cloud-api Postgres with immutable versions, view/comment/edit sharing, org admin settings and a public link route. Phase 1 server side is in; gizzi's artifact_* tools are feature:artifact-model-tools; the app (one ArtifactWindow, Artifacts tab, Share dialog, Output picker, public page /a/<id>) is in allternit-ai.

decisions.note: Eoj approved the share reference and preview: a compact owner/access-avatar pill with a dark Share action, and a rounded sharing panel with inline role pickers, people list and copy confirmation. Shared styling covers the v2 artifact window on Desktop, web phone and PWA plus the legacy Cowork private/org pane. Access avatars use saved grants, separate from live presence. Existing owner/policy rules and phone/PWA read-only sharing remain; no new public access is enabled.

Every Make something new tile opens an artifact session (Eoj: dashboards, motion and page opened no session; the others had no working pane). Kinds without an Office/Design editor (dashboard, motion, page, build, image, video, research) open a studio pane: empty state, then a rendering card shaped like the result (img-fx mosaic for image/video, skeleton + working beam otherwise) with the agent's live thought and tool steps, then the result in its ArtifactWindow with the kind's editor. Dashboard/Motion/Page sessions bind to the artifact their agent makes (artifact_create, then artifact_update). media_generate shows the same card inline in chat. Design canvas drops tldraw's menu/helper/share chrome, shows the style panel only with a selection or drawing tool, and follows the app theme.

Artifact toolbar and inline mode tabs use the UI font, a single horizontally scrolling row, and neutral glass selection across Desktop, web phone and PWA; reduced transparency and increased contrast get solid selection surfaces.

Eoj accepted the artifacts v2 contract (docs/design/artifacts-v2.md): one typed store in cloud-api under /api/v2/artifacts, private by default, links refused for artifacts that use AI or connectors, owner-only permanent delete, legacy stores import as runtime_version 1.

Page runtime (Phase 4a): page artifacts run in the MCP sandbox-proxy origin with connect-src none and window.allternit.{storage, ai, connectors}. Storage is 20 MB per artifact (personal per viewer, shared for all viewers, consent before the first shared write). AI is billed to the viewer through the hosted model router. Connector calls run in the app with the viewer's credentials via the MCP Apps bridge; tools that ask before each action are unavailable in pages. Outside invitees never get AI or connectors. The org Artifacts settings (Desktop and web only; phone and PWA show a note) include a connector kill switch and a Shared outside review list.

Phase 4 editors: doc, sheet, slides and design open in the window's editors with autosave to versions, Edit with Allternit on a selection, threaded comments with @gizzi, heartbeat presence (honours the org presence switch), and Word/PDF/Markdown/PowerPoint/XLSX/CSV/HTML/zip exports. Presence is a heartbeat poll under /api/v2/artifacts/:id/presence, not the deployment WebSocket hub.

Design artifacts open on the Design studio canvas (DesignTldrawCanvas with the Layers and Properties panels) scoped to one artifact, saved as a versioned canvas document (artboards, layers, design-system ref); older HTML designs open read-only with Convert to canvas. Phone and PWA use the canvas without tldraw chrome and the panels as bottom sheets. Presence is durable in artifact_presence (migration 086) so it works across cloud-api instances.

The Artifacts tab regained what the Phase 1 rebuild dropped: the animated Make something new tiles are the one template gallery (every kind, plan-gated, Dashboards and Motion included), connected-tools chips, the Design menu and Office button, and real per-kind previews in the grid (body fetched lazily, script-free snapshots for pages, designs and cards).

Craft editors Phase 1: `pdf` joins the kind contract (default body format application/pdf) on both sides — cloud-api KINDS allow-list and the app registry. PDFs open in the workspace through the embedded PdfCraft WASM editor over the craft:1 postMessage bridge served from office.allternit.com/craft/pdf/ (see feature:craft-editors). .pdf uploads become pdf-kind records.

features.label: Dashboards (live tiles that query your connectors)
features.description: Artifacts v2 dashboard kind: a 12-column grid of KPI, line, area, bar and table tiles, each carrying its own connector query (or read-only SQL for a warehouse). Runs as the viewer through the MCP Apps bridge with first-use approval that follows the account, cached first paint, refresh on open/interval/filter, click-to-see-query and per-tile errors. Edited by chat (artifact_update) or by hand (rename, reorder, resize). Paid plans; Desktop, phone layout and the PWA (stacked to one column). Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks and ClickHouse are listed in the connector directory.

decisions.note: Body is application/vnd.allternit.dashboard+json v1 (dashboards saved as OpenUI cards still open as cards). Queries reuse the card tool client: read-only tools only, plus one read-only SELECT through a warehouse SQL tool. First-use approval is saved to the account (the page-runtime connectors consent, with per-tool off in denied_tools) and localStorage is only a first-paint cache; signed-out viewers get no connectors. The owner's client declares capabilities.connectors so link sharing is refused. Warehouses with a per-account address (Snowflake, Databricks) or a self-run server (Redshift) are listed as setup guides, not invented endpoints. PDF export prints the dashboard; PNG export captures the rendered grid with modern-screenshot.

features.label: Motion artifacts (animated explainers, MP4 export)
features.description: The motion artifact kind: short animated compositions (title, counter, chart, logo, list scenes) stored as JSON props, drawn by a pure seekable renderer, edited in the artifact window (scene list, scrub, play/pause/loop, props panel; tabs on the phone layout and PWA) and exported to MP4. Desktop encodes frames with the local ffmpeg through the motion IPC; web and PWA encode in the tab with WebCodecs (MP4, or WebM where the browser has no H.264). Where the browser can't encode H.264, or on request (Export MP4 (cloud)), the cloud-api host renders the saved version with the same renderer bundled for Node (@napi-rs/canvas + ffmpeg): /api/v2/artifacts/:id/render, 2 renders at once, 3 per user, 1920x1080 and 120 s at 30 fps, 24 h files. Super, Ultra and Team plans; org default Team on, Enterprise off.

decisions.note: No server-side render route: no cloud render worker exists, so web and PWA export in the tab (WebCodecs + mediabunny) and Desktop uses local ffmpeg. Videos are silent. The body is data only, never code.

Cloud render added (supersedes the no-server-render ruling above for browsers without H.264 and for long clips): one renderer, the app's renderFrame bundled for Node into a vendored dist/render.mjs (regenerated by scripts/build-motion-render.mjs), run as a child process of cloud-api (node + @napi-rs/canvas + ffmpeg) under /api/v2/artifacts/:id/render. Jobs in motion_render_jobs (087). Files go to R2 when configured, else the host temp dir, deleted after 24 h. Same plan rule as Motion (Super, Ultra, Team). Desktop keeps local ffmpeg; the in-tab WebCodecs path stays the fast option.

features.label: Artifact tools for every model (Artifacts v2)
features.description: artifact_create / artifact_update / artifact_read built into gizzi-code for every model, and for CLI agents over the session MCP bridge. They save to cloud-api /api/v2/artifacts with the session's credential; without one, the result carries the full payload with persisted:false and the app saves it under the same id.

decisions.note: Contract docs/design/artifacts-v2.md section 5: create an artifact when content is substantial (~15+ lines), self-contained, likely edited or reused, or asked for. gizzi mints art_+ULID ids; 409 stale_version makes the model read, merge and retry.

features.label: Craft editors (embedded WASM editors over craft:1)
features.description: The vendored craft editors (PdfCraft, PhotoCraft, FilmCraft) run sandboxed in cross-origin iframes served from office.allternit.com/craft/<app>/ and speak the craft:1 postMessage protocol with the workspace host page: token-validated handshake, craft:open with transferable bytes, craft:save-request -> host persists -> craft:save-ack, and a craft:command channel so agents drive the same visible editor. Phase 1 (2026-10-10) wired the pdf kind end to end; Phase 2 (2026-10-10) wired the image kind: PhotoCraft opens the stored layered source (.pcraft/PSD in artifact runtime storage) when there is one, saves the source back to storage, flattens a PNG per save that becomes the new artifact version (R2 URL body), and gains a Download PSD export. Phase 3 (2026-10-10) is live: the video kind opens in the embedded FilmCraft editor (VideoCraftEditor over the same bridge; the video embed loads ?empty=1 so FilmCraft skips its demo project), the project source (.fcproj) round-trips through artifact runtime storage (craft/source.fcproj, personal scope), footage is a media-plane ref in meta.media (never bytes in the 20 MB text budget), the user's save requests an MP4 export (file.exportMedia) whose uploaded URL becomes the new text/uri-list version body, media_generate videos and uploaded video files land as video-kind artifacts, and the phone/PWA surfaces get view + an Edit entry to the full editor (trim-adapted phone UX is not claimed). The editor bundles serve cross-origin from office.allternit.com only — there is no allternit-ai public/craft mirror (the earlier note claiming one was wrong; image/pdf never had one either).

decisions.note: Phase 1 approved: pdf artifact kind + host-side craft:1 bridge (src/components/craft/bridge.ts) + CraftEditor wrapper + pdfjs read-only preview in the kind registry. The editor iframe 404s until the office.allternit.com/craft/pdf/ bundle deploys, so the allternit-ai PR stays unmerged until Eoj approves that deploy. Protocol: vendor/craft/craft-host/PROTOCOL.md (craft:1).

Phase 2 approved: image kind gets CraftEditor app=image (ImageCraftEditor). Save routing by save-request extension: user .pcraft/.psd saves -> artifact runtime storage (craft/source.pcraft, craft/source.psd) via the existing /api/v2/artifact-runtime storage routes, whose kind gate now admits image/video with a declared storage capability (Denied::NotStorageKind otherwise); host-requested app.save {path} exports (meta.path correlation) -> flattened PNG uploaded to Allternit Cloud file storage becomes the new text/uri-list version body. Bridge save-requests now pass the app's meta through. New Upload image in the library. Server: allternit-cloud-api runtime.rs allowed(); app: src/components/craft/image-io.ts + CraftEditor.tsx, src/lib/artifacts/runtime-storage.ts.

Phase 3 app-independent parts: `video` joins the kind contract — cloud-api KINDS gains the kind (default body format application/vnd.allternit.video+json) and the app registry gains the allow-list entry (interim rendering as code; no editor until the host-wiring slice). The craft_store runtime gate already admitted image|video (PR #1477), so no server gate change was needed. FilmCraft bundle rebuilt cleanly with CRAFT_FEATURES=embed (the video xtask forwards CRAFT_FEATURES to cargo --features; documented in vendor/craft/VENDOR.md for the future CI job) and published to office.allternit.com/craft/video/ plus mirrored into allternit-ai public/craft/video/. Server: cmd/allternit-cloud-api/src/artifacts/kinds.rs; app: src/lib/artifacts/{types,kinds}.ts.

Phase 3 host wiring: VideoCraftEditor (src/components/craft/CraftEditor.tsx) + video-io.ts. Open ladder: stored craft/source.fcproj wins, with the footage bytes re-imported under the same virtual path so a stored project's clip references resolve (the editor's file table is per-session; OPFS restore helps the same browser); first-time opens import the footage the meta.media ref points at and the host issues file.saveAs {path} so the app's own Save never prompts. Save routing by name extension (FilmCraft's adapter sends no format; meta.path is the virtual path): .fcproj -> runtime storage + a host-requested file.exportMedia {path} MP4 export; the export's save-request -> uploadAttachmentToCloud -> new text/uri-list version body with meta.media = {url, mime}; anything else (audio stems, caption sidecars) -> craft/export.<ext>. media_generate video outputs become video-kind drafts (project body + media-plane ref in meta) via from-transcript selectedToDraft; the library gains Upload video. Phone/PWA v1 is the playable view plus an Edit video entry that mounts the full FilmCraft (trim adaptation deferred, flagged). Bridge: video embeds load ?empty=1. Docs: guides/artifact-modes.mdx + docs/design/artifacts-v2.md app-contract bullet. Server untouched (the craft_store gate has admitted video since #1477). Office CSP fix (live bug the smoke caught): the #1475 _headers fix made script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' actually apply to /craft/* — and every vendored app's index.html boots from an INLINE script, so all three editors silently failed to boot (blank iframe, host handshake timeout; PDF/image/video alike, in-product verification had not caught it). Fixed by adding 'unsafe-inline' to the /craft/* script-src (surfaces/office.allternit.com/public/_headers): the office origin carries no credentials, apps run in opaque-origin sandboxed iframes, and connect-src 'none' + COOP/COEP remain. A live boot check (handshake -> craft:open -> command round-trip against the deployed bundle) is now documented in vendor/craft/VENDOR.md as required for the future CI job — strings|grep craft:1 does not catch a CSP-blocked boot. Live-boot fixes the smoke caught (nothing had ever booted the embed end-to-end; CSP only started applying with #1475's _headers-at-root fix): (1) office /craft/* CSP — script-src gains 'unsafe-inline' (vendored index.html files boot from inline scripts; a hash would churn per build), connect-src 'self' (the same-origin .wasm fetch), plus Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin (the sandboxed iframe's opaque origin module-loads its own glue/wasm). (2) bridge.ts speaks the crate's actual wire: bare kebab-case types (hello, open, save-request — no craft: prefix) and numeric command ids — the two sides were written against PROTOCOL.md independently and never integrated; PROTOCOL.md now documents the real wire. (3) Host→app posts must target '*' (explicit origins are never delivered to opaque-origin windows); app→host arrive with origin 'null' and the host pins event.source to its own iframe. (4) craft-host's wasm transport dropped EVERY [json, ArrayBuffer] message (the string-only parse returned early), so no craft:open bytes ever reached any app — fixed in the crate (Allternit-authored, not upstream) and the FilmCraft bundle rebuilt with CRAFT_FEATURES=embed. The image/pdf bundles embed the same latent transport bug and must be rebuilt the same way (same crate, no code change) before their editors can open documents — flagged follow-up, not done here to avoid redeploying live surfaces outside this slice. The future CI job must run a live boot check (handshake → open with bytes → one command), not just strings|grep craft:1.

features.label: Agency Kernel configuration
features.description: Shared responsive kernel dashboard with scoped rules, frozen schema inspection, decision policy navigation, model routing and installed capabilities. Availability follows the connected runtime.

decisions.note: Unify five kernel areas; retain canonical S0 Commands / S1 Decisions / S2 Generate / S3 Solve. Network and privacy controls reuse enforced fence, approvals and scoped local-only routing; no unsupported retention or firewall claims.

features.label: Agency Descent (decision flywheel)
features.description: Agency work moves down the tiers as it repeats: open-weight and trained decision heads, opt-in training data (per-org consent, DLP-redacted, shared heads), the Descent dashboard (tier mix, cheap share, escalations, oracle spend) and memory recall in Agency runs.

decisions.note: Training data is opt-in per organization; trained decision heads are shared across opted-in organizations; open-weight baselines instead of paid decision vendors; cloud test first. No GPU: trained heads train and run on CPU.

C2 + C5: a deterministic trace monitor checks every terminal run (no sampling) and stores findings (GET /v1/runs/:id/findings); an optional trace.error decision, labelled by the deterministic verdict, lets a head learn it later. Evals are trajectory graders over recorded-only replays or the scripted runner (/v1/evals/*), with regression cases promoted from runs and a manual CI gate (scripts/agency-eval-gate.mjs, 2 pp drop / any high-stakes failure). Replay and eval live model calls count against the same daily spend caps as runs.

Live S1 decisions in all six Agency graphs (journaled, never re-decided); CPU-trained decision heads (head.embed over EmbeddingGemma 2, head.rules compiled to S0) trained as background jobs on pooled opted-in data; replay overrides and replay-backed acceptance for head promotion; entity pages in memory recall; harness learning (C6): workflow edits proposed by deterministic operators or the planner model, scored on evals + recorded-only replays, accepted by a VERA-style rule and versioned only after human approval, with rollback.

features.label: Background tasks pane
features.description: Code sessions list everything the agent delegated (background shells and subagents, background or foreground) in a Tasks pane with live status, a running count on the pane strip, Stop, and each task's live output or subagent transcript.

decisions.note: Claude Code parity: one SessionTasks list (gizzi GET /session/:id/tasks, proxied as /agent-sessions/:id/tasks) merges durable BackgroundTask rows with foreground subagent child sessions. Bash gains run_in_background (kind "shell", 64KB live output tail, background.task.updated events, killed by cancel). background.task.* now reach the /sync feed as `background_task`.

cloud-api relays the task routes for ai.allternit.com. A TUI attached to a runtime session mirrors its shells and agents into the task table (ids tui_*, no daemon Bus events, so the pane refreshes every 10s); a surface's Stop settles the row and the TUI stops the task. Background-task restart cleanup now runs once per process and skips tui_* rows.

Code session pane selector is collapsed into a multi-select Panes menu with open-state checks and running-task count. Six code tool bodies share Browser shell surfaces on desktop, phone and popup. Terminal uses one tab bar with folder/branch context and bare shell chrome.

Claude CLI stream-json task lifecycle now mirrors into the same durable task list. Keep the owning CLI alive after its foreground result while tasks remain; poll bounded task output and forward targeted stop_task controls with acknowledgement. Missing terminal notifications become interrupted, never completed. No API shape or separate Desktop/phone implementation.

features.label: Code session file browser and editor
features.description: Code sessions keep a searchable folder tree beside tabbed file previews and editors, with hover/focus/touch Edit actions, session draft retention, save/error handling, and changed-file navigation into the editor across Desktop and both phone layouts.

decisions.note: Eoj requested the functional file workflow from Claude Desktop references, beyond pane colors. Added persistent tree/editor split, file tabs, hover Edit, responsive tree, unsaved-draft protection, file:line opening, grouped changes and full-hunk review. File API requests use current runtime routing and auth. Verified with file-workflow, editor, Changes, pane-manager, terminal, file API and console tests plus desktop/phone/dark layout review. Desktop needs its next build and the PWA needs its separate deployment.

features.label: Bots operate real phones
features.description: A bot sees and operates a real phone through one set of phone.* tools: a spare Android over Wi-Fi (adb + Google ARTEMIS), or an iPhone with an Allternit USB Agent (USB mouse/keyboard board + AirPlay mirror). Connected in Desktop; usable from every surface.

decisions.note: Lane 2a: Android over Wi-Fi with QR wireless-debugging pairing, adb downloaded and SHA-verified (never bundled), ARTEMIS sidecar for plain-English tasks; texts and calls need a native approval, are rate limited and block emergency numbers (#1197).
Old services/android-bridge connector retired: it needed a harness that exists only on one machine and its send_sms had no approval or rate limit (#1517).

Allternit USB Agent (Eoj named it): iPhone with no app, no Mac Mirroring and no developer account. ESP32-S3 USB HID board + UxPlay AirPlay receiver (GPL-3.0, separate process, PIN-protected) + calibration and closed-loop aiming adapted from esp32-iphone-agent (MIT). USBA/1: mutual HMAC handshake, per-connection session key, signed sequenced commands, boots disarmed, only the button arms it, lease and auto-disarm; key set only over USB. Same phone.* tools; phone.home/back/key added for both platforms. Not yet checked with a real board on Eoj's iPhone 17 Pro.
Opening Settings no longer downloads adb for people with no Android phone; the tool gateway starts on its own for iPhone-only users.

One-step setup: Desktop ships the USB Agent firmware (reproducible image + SHA-256 manifest, built by hardware/usb-agent/build-firmware.sh; source public, Eoj OK'd publishing) and Set up flashes it with esptool-js over Web Serial before writing Wi-Fi and the key. Desktop allows serial only for first-party pages and Espressif boards (VID 0x303A), auto-picked. Boards on older firmware show Update available.

Phone Link (SPEC-signed-in-apps-routing): bots use the AI apps already signed in on the user's own phone instead of vendor tokens (Sign in with ChatGPT removed, #1584). Desktop main state machine phone-link.ts + window.allternit.phoneLink IPC; Android USB to Wi-Fi in main, iPhone via an iCTRL fork set up over the cable is next. UI owned by the setup-flow track (onboarding 'Your AI' step + PhoneLinkSetup window).

Phone Link setup UI (ai, PhoneLinkSetup / PhoneLinkPanel / usePhoneLink): one screen per backend state with Eoj's per-state copy, Apple ID and 2FA forms that clear after submit and never log, a highlighted 'Turn on Developer Mode?' popup callout after the restart, and a result card listing each app's sign-in state. iPhone has no 'Coming soon': an unfinished backend step is a plain error. Opened from Settings > Subscriptions, Settings > Computers > Phones and onboarding Your AI ('Use the apps on your devices'; done only at ready_wifi). Web, phone layout and PWA show 'Set up from Allternit Desktop'.

iPhone helper signing with the user's own Apple ID, no Xcode: allternit-sideload sidecar (Rust over isideload 0.4.6, MIT), JSON lines over stdio with Desktop's SideloadSigner. Password only on stdin and zeroized; Apple session, signing key and anisette identity in the macOS Keychain (com.allternit.sideload) so re-signs skip password and 2FA. Stable per-team ids com.allternit.phonelink.<team> reuse App IDs; the runner's .xctest takes the runner's id (isideload's extension handling bypassed via its lower-level APIs; upstream PR drafted). Its own cargo workspace (russh 0.60.3 vs isideload aes-gcm conflict). OPTIONAL in packaging until anisette.allternit.com is hosted; hosting, licence review (apple-codesign-quick is LGPL-2.1) and Apple ToS are open.

Android Phone Link setup installs the Phone Link app over the cable (accessibility service, iCTRL protocol on :8200, starts on boot) instead of wireless debugging; linked phones are found again by device id when their Wi-Fi address changes.

In-app linked-Android live view (Phase 1): scrcpy-server pinned to v5.0.1 with a recorded SHA-256, downloaded on first use from the official release (never bundled); phone-scrcpy.ts implements the v5 wire protocol (dummy byte, 64-byte device name, h264 codec id, 12-byte session packets for rotation/size, 12-byte frame headers stripped before IPC), one shared PhoneStreamManager session per serial exposed to the renderer over phone:stream-* IPC with Annex-B H.264 chunks as structured-clone Buffers; input (touch/key/text/scroll/back/home/app_switch/power) and SET_DISPLAY_POWER encoded per control_msg.c. Agent-takeover banner: PhoneInfo.agentBusy fed by tool-runner and ARTEMIS activity counters. Streams start only on renderer request; the external scrcpy window stays a secondary action.

Settings → Computers → Phones labels each lane on its own: 'Screen & control' (adb + scrcpy, status 'Screen: …') and 'Phone Link — AI apps' (status 'Apps: …'), and a linked Android row says 'Screen not connected' while no phone is online on the screen lane — a healthy Phone Link pill had read as the whole phone being connected. Post-pair adb connect retries POST_PAIR_CONNECT_ATTEMPTS (4) times for mDNS lag and stops at once on cancel.

Bots reach Phone-Linked phones through one iCTRL lane in PhoneToolRunner (link: serials) with read_ui/find_and_tap/screen_text on every lane and per-phone health; remount and signature renewal are manual states.

Phone first (Eoj): Phone Link is the main way to connect an app; browser sign-ins are the fallback. Settings → Subscriptions opens with Link a phone and Linked phones (moved from Computers → Phones, which keeps a pointer plus the Android cable tools and the USB Agent), then Apps and channels: one row per app built only from live data (phone.devices apps + gateway accounts/providers + routes), never a UI list. The apps Phone Link looks for are data: surfaces/allternit-desktop/src/main/phone-app-catalog.json, 101 apps (the gateway's AI vendors with their provider ids, Telegram, and apps that have a connector, keyed by the connector id with its category), every store id checked against the App Store lookup API and Google Play (scripts/verify-phone-app-catalog.mjs). Desktop re-reads a healthy phone's apps every 10 min (Android replaces, iPhone only adds) and only ever probes AI chat apps by launching them. Connector detail pages say which linked phones have the app. No 'coming soon' rows. With Linked phones out of Computers → Phones, its 'Screen not connected' line is dropped; the 'Apps:' pill stays.

Phone Link helpers join the customer's Headscale mesh with embedded userspace tsnet (no OS VPN slot); keys come from /api/v1/mesh/enroll (Desktop passing them at cable setup is the next step); relays are our own DERP. tsnet log uploads to Tailscale are switched off in every Allternit mesh node (phones and the gizzi mesh-node sidecar). Live 2026-10-17: moto controlled from France over the mesh on LTE with Wi-Fi off.

iPhone Phone Link helper 1.98.12-allternit.2 (published + pinned) joins the user's mesh via sealed config; only local clients may use the one-shot pairing grant. Live 2026-10-17: iPhone on a phone hotspot (different network, no cable, helper started on the phone) driven from France over the mesh: ChatGPT opened, read_ui 208 lines, plaintext pairing over the mesh refused (403). Production mesh isolates customers (autogroup:self) since the same day. Android 0.2.1 runs the mesh in its own process.

Bot voice on a linked phone (CONTRACT-linked-phone-voice-2026-10-18): a call cable from the phone's headset port to a USB sound card on the Mac running Desktop. Desktop answers after one ring (Android adb KEYCODE_CALL, iPhone tap Accept via iCTRL, best effort), joins LiveKit room call-lp-<uuid> as linked-phone-<deviceId>, and the allternit-voice worker runs the bot as for a SIP call. Per-phone callBridge settings (Settings > Subscriptions > Linked phones > Call audio); call.started gains an optional line field; same CallScreen + phone-mirror switch on all three surfaces. dtmf/transfer/hold unsupported in v1. Bluetooth HFP (Moto) and iPhone Continuity were dropped first.

iPhone setup signs in with the Mac's own AuthKit anisette headers (allternit-sideload mac_anisette.rs; remote anisette only as fallback) because Apple now answers -80045 to emulated-device anisette servers. 2FA can be texted (two_factor_sms / submitTwoFactor('sms')), setup removes older Allternit helpers before install (free Apple ID 3-app limit), iOS 26 launch 'Error code: 2' reads as untrusted developer, and any linked phone can be removed (phone-link:remove). Live E2E on iPhone iOS 26.6.2 recorded by Eoj the same day.

Linked iPhones get a live screen as real video, Android-style (Eoj: smooth video mandatory, screenshot streaming not acceptable). iCTRL fork adds a ReplayKit Broadcast Upload Extension (iCTRLBroadcast, VideoToolbox H.264 30 fps) that feeds the runner over loopback 127.0.0.1:8203; the runner serves GET /video?ticket= as typed packets (STATUS/CONFIG/FRAME/ENDED) and start_live_screen/live_screen_status/stop_live_screen RPCs. Desktop IosVideoSession (phone-ios-video.ts) is a StreamSessionHandle for serial link:<deviceId>, so PhoneStreamManager, phone:stream-* IPC and the WebCodecs decoder are shared; input becomes tap/long_press/swipe/type/home RPCs. allternit-ai: liveScreenSerial() opens healthy iPhones in the phone frame. iOS requires a Start Broadcast tap per broadcast; the runner automates it via XCUITest when it can.

Turned phones: iPhone CONFIG rotation travels as PhoneStreamMeta.rotation and the viewer draws the frame upright (allternit-ai rotation.ts), sending input back in the video's own portrait pixels so old and new viewers agree. Simulator probe: the runner's synthesized tap/drag/swipe use that fixed portrait space in any orientation, XCUICoordinate uses the rotated one, so long_press goes fast when turned and Back swipes from the app's left edge. A mid-stream size change re-sends meta through PhoneStreamManager to Desktop, web and PWA viewers.

Eoj: phone apps must show the same telemetry as browser sign-ins. Read-only account reader (taps only menu labels, deny-list, never types) reads account, plan and usage windows every 6 h on an idle unlocked phone; new ACCESSIBILITY_OFF health state replaces a false HEALTHY.

Every app on a linked phone gets a check (signed in + account; plan and usage where the app shows them), not only AI chat. iPhone paths verified screen by screen with every Settings page scrolled: ChatGPT Settings > Usage and limits (Weekly), Gemini Settings > Usage limits (Current + Weekly), Claude, plus Discord, Telegram, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X, YouTube and GitHub accounts; per-app account rules so feed handles are never taken; drawer says Verified reader. A renewal-window iPhone whose signature hasn't lapsed now counts as working (it was treated as offline).

features.label: Phone stream relay (Phones 2.0)
features.description: Any surface views and controls a linked Android through the account's Desktop app: the browser opens /ws/phones/:serial/stream with a short-lived HMAC token (purpose phone_stream, read-only by default, ACI-gated full control, 4401 close at expiry), and the Desktop's phone-link session socket (/ws/phone-link/session, desktop-credential auth) relays the scrcpy H.264 stream and JSON control envelopes both ways. Registry is in-memory in allternit-api; cloud PG registered_phones rows (identity + last_seen only) are the persistence, so GET /api/v1/phones can say "linked but Desktop offline".

decisions.note: Phones 2.0 relay lane (approved plan): mirrors the computer_ws VNC proxy minus VNC — frames are opaque (binary video + JSON text). Read-only is enforced at the pipe (a read-only token's browser->desktop frames are dropped) because the payload is never parsed. One active stream per phone-link socket: a socket may hello many phones (all register online) but streams one serial at a time; scrcpy is one device per process, so the Desktop opens one socket per streamed phone. Full-control tokens reuse the computer_ws ACI confirmation-grant pattern.

features.label: Local vendor bot adapters
features.description: Connections for 31 of the 33 pictured bot projects: native vendor APIs (OpenMausBot, Codync, Hivekeep, Invisible Dots, CopilotKit OpenDots/OpenMuse/OpenBot, DS Bot, Nightly OpenBot, Rakazo, FrockBot, Sidemates, nanoMuse, Vellum Assistant, Open Dots by Anil, Gawkbot, Munder Difflin, Happy), browser sign-in (Gemini Spark, Slashy, AbacusAI), macOS Messages (Iris, Poke, Instinct, Flip, Cue, Pally), and existing vendors (Grok Bot, OpenAI Dots, Muse, Cadu via Hermes). Noodle and Omnibots are on hold. Live account verification is pending.

decisions.note: Catalog identification is separate from implemented connections. Native adapters match vendor requests and refuse unsupported control capabilities.

Coverage of all 33 pictured projects is settled: a connector only where the vendor's own source exposes authenticated bot discovery, send and attributable replies. Hosted apps without an API, session-cookie-only, end-to-end-encrypted, keystroke-driven and unauthenticated projects are marked No supported connection instead of being proxied.

Eoj: every project should connect. Browser sign-in and Messages routes are used where no API exists; projects that would need a large separate bridge (Noodle's QUIC Hub link) or reverse engineering (Omnibots) are on hold.

Eoj: all connected bots must talk together in group chats and look like their own product. Vendor members now answer inline in rooms through their connector with the room history (one standing thread per room), never a native model; each connector has its own look pack (brand accent + logo; Messages assistants use an iMessage face). allternit-api routes direct connectors by vendor id (DIRECT_ADAPTER_VENDORS) so account discovery works.

features.label: Desktop pets and animated avatars (Petdex standard)
features.description: Bot avatars play Petdex-standard sprite sheets (8 columns of 192x208, 11 rows: idle, running-right/left, waving, jumping, failed, waiting, running, review, sleep, special). Characters without real frames hop, rock, slump and spin in code (PortraitPetMotion). One pet-activity signal (lib/agents/pet-activity.ts) follows every session store and bot/vendor thread. In-app avatars (rail, headers, surface mascot, A:// orb) react to it. The Desktop pet window gets that state over IPC from the main window and plays it (walk rows while roaming), with a mail badge for replies that finished while you were away; click opens quick chat, double-click shows or hides the app. Terminal agents drive the same pet through a token-guarded loopback hook port (127.0.0.1:7787; gizzi built in, a hook script for Claude Code and Codex), and the pet shows speech bubbles in a click-through window above it. The free character builder renders Petdex v2 sheets with walk rows turned toward the direction of travel.

decisions.note: Eoj approved the desktop pet plan (8 PRs) after seeing Hermes Agent + Petdex. Sheets adopt the Petdex standard. Avatars without real frames hop (free approach). Muse in Gizzi Brawl is Jolly. Hook port 127.0.0.1:7787, not shared with anything else. Plan: agent-ledger/summaries/2026-10-15-2245-claude-desktop-pets-petdex.md.

Eoj approved the full-size code-drawn Gizzi YouTube rig sheets ("yes they are right"). PR 2 ships them plus Gemini, Muse and Muse Wonder as Petdex v2 sheets, swapped in place at the same URLs so saved bots upgrade.

Phase 3: every Gizzi Brawl fighter and Super form redrawn as a Petdex v2 sheet and swapped in at the same URLs; Super Codex, Super Grok and Gizzi Lightning added to the pack. Eoj asked for ChatGPT-dots-style characters in Dot Friends "like theirs but our own" so users recognise them: Bleu, Lily, Sunny, Rosie added with v2 sheets.

features.label: One-click install and sign-in for CLI brains
features.description: Settings → Connections → Coding tools installs CLI brains (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, …) on the active computer with the Factory's pinned, licence-gated installer (private Node when the machine has none), then signs in with a link and code shown on any device, so a cloud computer can run them while the user's Mac is off.

decisions.note: Eoj: build plan step D (Install → Sign in → Connected for any computer) so his always-on cloud computer can run CLI brains. Reuses the Factory harness installer, not a second manifest; sign-in captures the CLI's own link/code instead of opening a browser nobody sees.

Eoj: show and support every popular coding CLI and let people add an unlisted one through the same channels. One catalog file (cli-catalog.json, 38 tools) now feeds gizzi's brains and allternit-api; custom CLIs (argv only, no shell) are accepted only on single-owner runtimes (Desktop, self-hosted).

features.label: Gateway /v1/embeddings proxies to a configured provider
features.description: POST /v1/embeddings on the LLM gateway no longer stops at fake-or-501: when ALLTERNIT_GATEWAY_EMBED_URL names an OpenAI-compatible backend the operator runs (self-hosted or cloud), validated requests are proxied transparently and status, body, model id, and usage all come from the provider. Unset keeps the safe 501 allternit.not_configured; the hash-fake path stays fenced behind ALLTERNIT_GATEWAY_ALLOW_FAKE_PROVIDERS=1. The end-user `user` field is accepted but never forwarded upstream.

decisions.note: Eoj: embeddings must route through the gateway API like chat does. Gateway-specific env (ALLTERNIT_GATEWAY_EMBED_URL) instead of memory_index's ALLTERNIT_EMBED_URL so the public surface stays 501-unconfigured by default and never silently points at a sidecar.

features.label: Attention alerts (no silent failures)
features.description: Server-owned alerts: every failed, missed or bot-less routine (and later a down lane, a loop guard hold or a held send) opens one attention item, pushes it, re-notifies until fixed and shows in the needs-you inbox with Retry and Dismiss.

decisions.note: Agent-network Phase 1 WP1 (SPEC-agent-network-phase1-2026-10-16): alerts move from a client poller to the runtime; routine.failed is pushed only as attention.opened. Eoj: SMS for critical alerts is opt-in, off by default (not built yet).

features.label: Sign-in screen
features.description: The sign-in and sign-up pages on the web, the Desktop first-run, terminal login and the phone/PWA sign-in screen, with the sign-in stage (an auto-looping preview of the four real views: Home, Bots, Code, ACI) beside the real Clerk sign-in rail.

Desktop, ai.allternit.com (desktop and phone layouts) and the m.allternit.com PWA.

features.label: Console sign-in and developer setup
features.description: platform.allternit.com sign-in/sign-up with the looping API/Models/Compute/Runs previews, and the first-run setup for new accounts (organization, where workloads run, API key, first call, plan) ending in a connected view of the account.

features.label: Meet your bots onboarding card
features.description: First-run setup's Main bot step and the first visit to Bot Mode: the Bots network, a team picked from the bot templates (drag onto a grid or tap), the main bot (A:// by default), the team's routines on the editable scheduler, and a guided first job. Shown once per account.

journeys.label: Answer with a live data card
journeys.description: From a question to a card that reads your connected app and, with your approval, changes it.

steps.says: On send, the app adds the interactive-answers manual (with your connector tools) to the turn's system prompt, unless Settings says Text only.
gizzi-code appends it to its own system prompt and the model replies with an openui fence.
The transcript splits the fence out and renders the card as it streams.
Query() runs a read-only tool through the MCP Apps bridge; a Mutation() waits for the Allow bar.
The bridge calls the connector with your own credentials and returns the result straight to the card, not the model.

journeys.label: Send a message, get a streamed reply
journeys.description: What happens between pressing send in chat and the first token appearing.

steps.says: You type in ai.allternit.com (or Desktop, or the phone layout).
The chat view sends the message.
The chat client opens the request and an event stream.
allternit-api records the turn.
allternit-api calls gizzi-code over HTTP for the model work; it never calls a provider directly.
gizzi-code routes to the chosen model provider.
Tokens stream back and render as they arrive.

journeys.label: Text your bot
journeys.description: A text to a bot's number reaches the bot on your computer and the reply goes back by SMS.

steps.says: The carrier posts the inbound text to the number's relay address.
The cloud API checks opt-in and queues the text for your runtime.
Your allternit-api picks it up from the relay.
The bot that owns the number handles it in its thread.
gizzi-code runs the bot's turn.
The reply leaves through the cloud API and the carrier.

journeys.label: Start a Factory team from your phone
journeys.description: From m.allternit.com to agents running in panes on your computer.

steps.says: You open Factory on m.allternit.com.
The phone shell shows the Factory screen.
You pick a team or template and start it.
allternit-api proxies the request to the Factory engine on that computer.
The engine starts the agents and tracks approvals.
Each agent runs in a pane you can watch live from the phone.

journeys.label: Get a cloud computer with a paid plan
journeys.description: From Stripe checkout to a desktop you can open in the workspace.

steps.says: Stripe's webhook tells the cloud API the plan is paid.
Provisioning creates the machine.
The new computer is recorded and paired to your account.
The computer boots with the Allternit runtime.
It appears in Computers, where you and your bots can open it.

journeys.label: Talk to a bot by voice
journeys.description: From pressing the mic to hearing the bot answer.

steps.says: You start voice mode.
The client picks a voice endpoint: local, or cloud with a ticket.
For cloud voice, the cloud API issues the ticket and records consent.
The voice service turns speech into text and back.
allternit-api runs the bot's turn and returns the reply to speak.

journeys.label: A bot remembers across surfaces
journeys.description: A note saved in one place is recalled by a bot somewhere else.

steps.says: You or a bot save a note to Memory Drive.
allternit-api stores it.
Nightly consolidation merges and links notes.
On a later turn, retrieval finds the relevant notes.
gizzi-code puts them in the bot's context.

journeys.label: Approve an MCP app's action
journeys.description: An app event that needs you, from the app to your approval.

steps.says: A connected MCP app sends an event.
The event feed marks it approval_required.
It lands in your Needs you inbox with an approve link.
You approve it in the workspace.
The bot it was waiting on carries on.

journeys.label: Customize a project or folder icon
journeys.description: From opening appearance controls to seeing the saved personal icon.

steps.says: Open Customize appearance from the project card options menu.
Edit folder/paper colors and the overlay; preview, save, cancel, reset or export.
Validate the recipe and send an authenticated request to the connected runtime.
Validate and persist the preference for this user; null resets it.
Refresh subscribers across the shared Desktop, web and phone UI.

journeys.label: Set up a new account
journeys.description: From the first signed-in launch to Home with a computer, a style, a default brain and a main bot.

steps.says: OnboardingGate (Desktop/web) or PhoneFirstRunGate (phone) asks the setup config whether this account finished setup.
Gizzi + A:// ask where it runs, style and default brain; each choice runs the real connect flow and prints a result card.
A subscription brain connects on the Sessions computer and needs the provider-terms disclosure before it becomes the default.
Step 4: the bot setup picker sets up the main bot (setUpPrimaryBot with the picked look and name) or connects/creates/imports a bot; Gizzi's card appears only on a real result.
Open Allternit saves onboardingComplete and the default model to the setup config, then Home shows.

journeys.label: New developer: sign in to first API call
journeys.description: From the console sign-in to a created org, a gateway key and a real first call.

steps.says: Clerk sign-in (GitHub, Google, email) beside the looping console previews.
On /, a sure-new account (no setup record, no org, no keys) is sent to /setup once.
Creates the Clerk org and sandbox project, a gateway key shown once, runs one real /v1/chat/completions call, picks a plan, then shows the connected view and opens the Dashboard.
